reviewer: Codex author review, unblinded and not independent expert validation.
scope: First case in frozen input order for each source/label stratum, independent of predictions; review every returned evidence item.
rubric: supported = grounded in message or saved check/tool output; partial = grounded core plus unverified claim; unsupported = contradicted or no supporting observation. Source checks are assessed for consistency, not independently re-fetched.
summary: Reviewed all 32 evidence items from seven selected cases: 21 supported, 10 partial, 1 unsupported. Main issues: unsupported .ru pricing/prevalence claim; assumed lack of prize entry; external/general claims presented as observed facts; static HTML checks overstated. Historical benign URL no longer resolves and historical phishing shortener returns 404. Failed-check statements can be supported statements of failure, not successful investigation. Registry claims were checked for consistency with saved results only; no site was fetched locally.

claims.finding: The message says an order shipped, tells the user to open the Amazon app directly for tracking, and contains no links, payment requests, or credential requests. No urgency or pressure.
claims.rationale: Directly matches the message; no linked site or credential request is present.

claims.finding: .ru domains are cheap and common in scam texts
claims.rationale: The .ru suffix is observable, but no pricing or scam-prevalence data supports the cheap/common claim.

claims.finding: No registration record found for refleksiya-absurda.ru
claims.rationale: Matches the saved automated RDAP no-record result. This is consistency with a check, not independent registry validation.

claims.finding: The link's domain does not resolve, so the page could not be opened and no content, forms, or brand could be checked.
claims.rationale: Saved sandbox result has ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED, ok=false and no page HTML.

claims.finding: The domain has no registration record in the registry, so its owner and creation date are unknown.
claims.rationale: No-record result is saved, but saying the domain has no registry record overstates a lookup that can lack coverage; ownership was not checked.

claims.finding: The message is only a bare web link, with no brand name, payment request, or urgency language to judge.
claims.rationale: Input is a bare URL without payment, brand or urgency wording.

claims.finding:
Couldn't open the link safely (Error: Page.goto: net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED at https://www.refleksiya-absurda.ru/
Call log:
  - navigating to "https://www.refleksiya-absurda.ru/", waiting until "domcontentloaded"
)
claims.rationale: Failure statement matches saved sandbox DNS error and is correctly marked ok=false.

claims.finding: The message is only a bare link with no explanation, brand, payment request or urgency, so its purpose is unclear.
claims.rationale: Bare URL and lack of explanatory context match input.

claims.finding: The message just asks for a room number so the sender can knock on the right door. It has no links, payment requests, or urgency.
claims.rationale: Room-number request and absence of links, payments and urgency match the text.

claims.finding: cutt.ly is a link shortener that hides the real destination
claims.rationale: Matches the shortener check and bare cutt.ly URL. It describes indirection, not proof of fraud.

claims.finding: cutt.ly was registered 8 years ago
claims.rationale: Matches saved RDAP check; exact registry response is not independently re-fetched.

claims.finding: Opening the link in a sandbox returned a cutt.ly '404 Page Not Found' error, so the real destination stayed hidden.
claims.rationale: Saved sandbox status 404 and title explicitly identify a Cuttly page-not-found error.

claims.finding: The returned page has no login, card, or ID forms, and no hidden redirects.
claims.rationale: Saved HTML has no form/input/meta-refresh tags; static parsing cannot exclude every hidden or script-driven redirect.

claims.finding: No brand names appear in the page text; the word 'apple' appears only in an icon link tag.
claims.rationale: Apple occurs in apple-touch-icon as claimed, but only a finite brand list was searched; the page itself carries Cuttly branding.

claims.finding: cutt.ly is an established link shortener, registered in January 2018.
claims.rationale: Eight-year age is in checks; January 2018 appears only in Droid self-report, without the raw tool return preserved.

claims.finding: The message is only a bare short link, with no context, amounts, or payment details.
claims.rationale: The entire input is the shortened URL with no amounts or payment context.

claims.finding: Opened in a sandbox: lands on cutt.ly ('404 Error - Page Not Found | Cuttly')
claims.rationale: Final URL and title match saved sandbox capture.

claims.finding: The message is only a bare shortened link with no explanation, sender context or stated purpose, leaving the recipient to click blind.
claims.rationale: Input is a bare shortened link without explanatory text.

claims.finding: Matches a known 'investment romance' scam pattern
claims.rationale: Text explicitly promises returns and demands an upfront withdrawal fee, supporting the investment pattern (romance is the combined category name).

claims.finding: Asks for payment via usdt — hard or impossible to reverse
claims.rationale: USDT request is explicit; reversibility claim is general payment knowledge, not a case-specific explorer or transaction check.

claims.finding: The message promises guaranteed 20% daily returns with zero risk, which no real investment can offer.
claims.rationale: 20% daily, guaranteed, zero-risk claims are quoted correctly; universal investment claim was not externally checked.

claims.finding: The message asks you to send USDT now, a crypto payment that is very hard or impossible to reverse.
claims.rationale: USDT urgency is explicit; reversal mechanics are not established by a supplied tool observation.

claims.finding: The message says you must pay a separate 'unlocking tax' before you can withdraw profits, a classic advance-fee trick.
claims.rationale: A separate tax before withdrawal is explicit; advance-fee characterization follows that structure.

claims.finding: The message contains no links, domains, phone numbers, or crypto wallet addresses, so there was nothing to open or look up.
claims.rationale: No actual URL, phone, domain or wallet address appears in the message; the word wallet is not an address.

claims.finding: The message pushes urgency with 'Send USDT now', promises 'guaranteed 20% daily returns, zero risk', and says you must pay a separate 'unlocking tax' to the sender's wallet before withdrawing profits.
claims.rationale: Accurately quotes the urgency, promised returns and withdrawal condition.

claims.finding: Matches a known 'prize lottery' scam pattern
claims.rationale: Prize and paid claim-call wording support the prize-lottery pattern.

claims.finding: The message claims a £400 prize and tells you to call a number at 10p per minute, a common premium-rate phone scam.
claims.rationale: Prize amount and 10p/minute charge are explicit; the finding characterizes that paid-claim pattern rather than a verified phone owner.

claims.finding: The phone number 087104711148 has 12 digits, but UK numbers starting with 0 normally have 11, so the number may be invalid or fake.
claims.rationale: 12 digits is verifiable from text, but UK numbering rule was not looked up. Droid summary explicitly admits reliance on general knowledge.

claims.finding: The message has no links, domains, email addresses, or crypto wallets, so there is no web page to open or check.
claims.rationale: No URL, email, domain or crypto address appears in input.

claims.finding: The message uses pressure tactics such as 'NOW', 'easy', and 'this is the 2nd time we have tried to contact you'.
claims.rationale: Quoted urgency phrases appear in input.

claims.finding: Claims you won £400 without any entry, says this is the '2nd time' they've tried to reach you, and demands you call a number 'NOW'.
claims.rationale: Prize and NOW are explicit; without any entry is invented context not established by the message.

claims.finding: Message claims you were 'awarded' a camera you never entered for, and tells you to call a phone number from a landline to claim it, with a delivery timeframe.
claims.rationale: Camera award and call instruction are explicit; you never entered is unsupported personal context.
